Use `useLayoutEffect` when you need to measure or change the DOM before the browser paints, such as reading an element's size to place a popover or setting scroll position, so the user never sees an in-between frame. Use `useEffect` for everything else (fetching, subscriptions, logging), since it runs after paint and doesn't block rendering.
Action: None.

Parking the timing work (I'm still waiting on which HTTP framework the api uses). Duplicate emails in the seed usually come from generating random emails independently, so collisions are possible, but I haven't read the script yet.
Action: Read the seed script, make emails unique (for example by using a deterministic suffix or tracking used values), and run the seed twice to confirm no unique index error.

Likely your docker CLI still points at the old Docker Desktop socket, via a docker context or a DOCKER_HOST setting. OrbStack provides its own context, so switching the context (or unsetting DOCKER_HOST) should fix compose, and it matters for the api tests too, since my notes say they run on Testcontainers and need Docker running.
Action: Check `docker context ls` and DOCKER_HOST, switch to the OrbStack context, confirm with `docker info`, then retry `docker compose up -d db redis`.

A form that posts twice on Enter usually has two things triggering it, for example both `hx-post` on the form and on the button, or an extra `hx-trigger` such as a keyup on top of the normal submit. I haven't seen the template, so I'm not certain which it is.
Action: Look at the add-hike form in trailmix, remove the duplicate trigger, and add `hx-sync="this:drop"` and `hx-disabled-elt` as a safety net.

Not really, a rename that ends with a clean typecheck is the easy kind. The `useActiveOrg` rename is done and `tsc` reports 0 errors with no references to the old name left.

Good call. Sums coming back as strings is typical when the database driver returns aggregate or numeric values as text, so they need a cast in SQL or a conversion in the mapper. I haven't looked at which driver or column types are involved.

The digest is a property Next puts on the error, and Sentry doesn't pick it up automatically, so it has to be attached explicitly when global-error.tsx reports.
Action: Update app/global-error.tsx to pass error.digest to Sentry as a tag and as extra data, and add a test or check that it is sent.

The date range is date-only, so I'll keep it as plain date strings and test under a few time zones, and InvoiceStatus now includes void.
Action: Move status, client and date range into search params, read them on load, use router.replace, and add tests.

They're different: HTTP/1.1 keep-alive only reuses one TCP connection, but requests on it still go one after another, which is why browsers open several connections in parallel. HTTP/2 multiplexing sends many requests at once as interleaved streams over a single connection and compresses headers, though TCP-level head-of-line blocking remains.
Action: None.

Action: Read apps/api/src/lib/invoice-number.ts, find the race, fix it atomically, and run the api tests in parallel repeatedly to confirm.

tsx uses esbuild to strip types and transform on the fly, with no type checking, so it starts fast. ts-node uses the TypeScript compiler API and type-checks by default, which is slower, and its ESM support has been rougher.
Action: Separately, the lockfile is still waiting on an install after adding tsx, tell me the command or I'll run the usual one from the repo root.

I'll add retry with exponential backoff to the CLI api client for 502, 503 and 504 only, 3 attempts total, and fail immediately on other statuses.

On the delete endpoint: DELETE /v1/customers/:id will set `deleted_at` (never a hard delete) and return errors as RFC 7807 problem+json. The lockDuration change stays parked for later.
Action: Implement the route scoped like the other customer routes, with 204 on success and problem+json for bad id and not found, then add tests and register it.

There is a real difference. structuredClone keeps Dates, Maps, Sets and typed arrays and handles circular references, while the JSON round trip turns Dates into strings, drops undefined and breaks on cycles. Neither copies functions.
Action: None.

`using x = resource` calls `x[Symbol.dispose]()` automatically when the scope exits, even on throw, and `await using` does the same with `Symbol.asyncDispose`. It needs the right target/lib settings, and the runtime may need Symbol.dispose to exist or be polyfilled.
Action: None.

The server rendered the due date as 'Sep 21, 2026' and the client as '21 Sept 2026', because the date was formatted with the user's locale, which differs between the server and the browser. React sees different text and throws a hydration error.
Action: Look at the InvoiceRow due-date cell, find the locale-dependent formatting, and make it deterministic (explicit locale and timezone on both sides).

The common thread is that each error is a type imported with a normal import, and verbatimModuleSyntax requires `import type { X }` or `import { type X }`. Both are the same fix, just repeated.
Action: Run the repo's linter autofix if it has an import-type rule, otherwise a codemod, then re-run tsc across the workspace.
